# Gene Editing Lowers Oxalate Output in Hyperoxaluria Patients

A single infusion of YolTech Therapeutics' in vivo editing therapy YOLT-203 reduced 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion by up to 62% at one year in 11 children and adults with primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1). Kidney function was unchanged across the follow-up period.

By: Gorm Palmgren - Oct. 26, 2026

title: US Orphan Drug Market USD 224.9 Billion by 2033
summary:
The FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research approved 46 novel drugs in 2025, of which 23 — exactly 50.0 per cent — carried Orphan Drug Designation. Between them, those 23 programmes were supported by 5,001 patients in the pivotal trials that took them to approval: 19.2 per cent of the roughly 26,000 pivotal participants behind all 46 approvals, at a mean of 217 and a median of 114 patients per programme.

Nine of the twenty-three were approved on a data set of a hundred patients or fewer.
